t.E418.agn: In 2018 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI); it reported that no adverse effects were seen in humans at intakes of up to 200 mg/kg body weight per day for 3 weeks. EFSA recommended better definition of the purity criteria (including the absence of viable cells of the producing bacterium).
t.E418.body: Gellan gum is not absorbed intact in the gut and is not fermented by gut bacteria.
t.E418.found.0: May be used in many foods in the EU at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E418.prod: Produced by fermentation with the bacterium Sphingomonas elodea.
t.E418.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed. Improvement of the purity criteria was recommended.
t.E418.regx.1: Group I additive; may not be used in jelly mini-cups.
t.E418.summary: A gelling agent produced by bacterial fermentation. It provides thickness and keeps particles in suspension in plant-based milks, desserts and drinks.
t.E418.what: It forms a gel, thickens and keeps the mixture stable.
